newsitem.title: USA: Former Miami, Fla, city manager pleads innocent.
newsitem.headline: Former Miami, Fla, city manager pleads innocent.

text.p: Former Miami City Manager Cesar Odio and a city lobbyist pleaded innocent Wednesday to six counts of conspiracy, embezzlement and witness tampering.
Odio and lobbyist Jorge Luis de Cardenas entered the pleas during a brief hearing before U.S. Magistrate Peter Palermo.

An indictment made public Tuesday charged that Odio and de Cardenas allegedly conspired with former Miami city manager Manohar Surana to embezzle city money through a contract with a health insurance company.
The indictment alleged they conspired to inflate the monthly insurance bill by $12,500 and divide the extra money among themselves. Both denied the charges.
Odio's attorney, Richard Sharpstein, said trial is expected early next year. Odio and de Cardenas remain free on bond.
Sharpstein said Odio never took any city money. He said the money paid to de Cardenas was a legitimate lobbying fee, and was paid by the health insurance company, not the city.
If convicted of the charges, Odio and de Cardenas face up to 35 years in prison.
Prosecutors said Surana has agreed to plead guilty to unspecified charges and was cooperating with investigators.

Former city commissioner Miller Dawkins has already pleaded guilty to accepting $75,000 from a computer company seeking a city contract. He is free pending sentencing in January and faces up to 10 years in prison.
